title: Deep single-cell immune- and signaling profiles predict therapy response in chronic myeloid leukemia within hours

key_results: Single-cell immune and signaling profiles from first dose predicted 12-month BCR::ABL1IS response; dasatinib response driven by leukemic burden, neutrophil maturity (pSTAT3 Y705), and immune effector activity (pERK in T/NK cells); nilotinib response driven by LSC-like cell signaling (cleaved caspase-3, pCRKL Y207, STAT3); distinct drug-specific signatures reflect kinase specificity beyond BCR::ABL1
comments: Remarkable finding: single-cell signaling within 1–3 hours predicts 12-month outcome; drug-specific predictive features suggest mechanistic understanding and optimization potential.

model_io.model: Mass cytometry analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes with single-cell immune and signaling profiles
inputs: PBL from de novo CML patients on first day of TKI treatment (dasatinib or nilotinib)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Drug-specific immune and signaling profiles within hours of first dose predict 12-month treatment response better than baseline prognostic factors
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: single-cell profiles predictive for both dasatinib and nilotinib with distinct mechanistic signatures

title: Supervised deep learning for efficient cryo-EM image alignment in drug discovery with cryoPARES
task: Accelerate cryo-EM particle alignment for drug discovery using deep learning
key_results: cryoPARES achieves angular predictions significantly faster than traditional methods; enables near real-time reconstructions with automated particle pruning; rapid structural determination of seven ligand-bound complexes across four protein targets
comments: Transfer learning from pre-aligned datasets is pragmatic for high-throughput screening, though generalization to novel protein classes requires validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Prior pose information from equivalent protein samples improves alignment speed without sacrificing accuracy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: achieves rapid predictions and automated pruning enabling real-time feedback during data acquisition

title: DEGAS, disease endophenotyping through graph and adjacency metrics: network biomarkers for Parkinson’s disease progression
task: Identify network-defined PD subtypes using functional connectivity and graph metrics
key_results: DEGAS models incorporating graph theory achieved balanced accuracy 0.91–0.93 (MCC 0.61–0.78), outperforming adjacency-only models (0.79 accuracy, MCC 0.52); sRBD-positive patients showed worse motor outcomes, accelerated autonomic dysfunction, and higher rates of hallucinations/dyskinesias/depression
comments: Graph metrics capture basal ganglia-thalamic, temporal-limbic, and cerebello-cortical circuits; external validation required before clinical deployment.

model_io.model: DEGAS: classifiers integrating adjacency matrices and graph theory metrics from fMRI
inputs: baseline fMRI from 336 early-stage PD patients

hypotheses.hypothesis: Graph theory features encoding brain circuit topology identify PD subtypes with distinct clinical trajectories better than adjacency patterns alone
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: graph-based models significantly outperformed adjacency-only models; sRBD-positive group had worse outcomes

title: Multi-omic integration identifies sex-dependent molecular targets in Parkinson’s disease
task: Identify sex-dependent molecular targets in Parkinson's disease through multi-omic integration
key_results: 102 candidates across 31 loci prioritized; 11 genes significant across three layers (SNCA, MAPT, CTSB in both sexes; CD160, L3MBTL2 male-specific; GPNMB, LRRC37A2 male-predominant; STX4, PRSS53 female-predominant); sex-divergent pathways (male: immune signaling/SUMOylation; female: chromatin remodeling)
comments: Sex-stratified analysis reveals previously unreported male-specific candidates and distinct molecular pathways, strengthening case for sex-aware therapeutic development.

model_io.model: Gene-based association, TWAS, PWMR with colocalization, MR with eQTLs

hypotheses.hypothesis: Sex-stratified multi-omic integration reveals sex-dependent molecular contributions to PD susceptibility layered on shared lysosomal/α-synuclein axes
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: identified sex-specific candidates (CD160, L3MBTL2) and sex-divergent pathways

title: Regularized ensemble polygenic risk prediction with GWAS summary statistics

key_results: Ensemble PRS framework integrating large candidate models using only summary statistics outperforms state-of-the-art within and across ancestries; enables seamless integration of newly developed models with existing ones; addresses limitation requiring individual-level genotype data
comments: Scalable solution for PRS development leveraging summary statistics; particularly valuable for non-European populations with insufficient genomic samples.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Regularized ensemble combining multiple PRS models from summary statistics improves predictive accuracy within and across ancestries
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: ensemble approach outperformed state-of-the-art single-model PRS methods

title: A zero-shot spillover denoiser for highly multiplexed images

comments: Zero-shot unsupervised approach using optimal transport is innovative; released as standalone script and Fiji plugin for accessibility.

no training data or additional experiments required

hypotheses.hypothesis: Optimal transport theory identifies similar patches across channels to retain true signal while removing noise and spillover without ground truth
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: SpillOT outperformed zero-shot baselines; enabled detection of immune infiltration patterns previously undetectable

title: Transforming molecular evolutionary analyses with protein foundation models
task: Articulate protein foundation models as tools for evolutionary analysis and functional inference

comments: Synthesis paper articulating pFM evolutionary foundations; individual sequence analysis bypasses traditional comparative requirements, though limitations and open questions regarding routine application remain.

comments: Multi-omic integration (microbiome + transcriptomics) elegantly rules out bacterial etiology and identifies specific iron metabolism dysregulation; suggests inadequate dietary iron absorption.

comments: Rigorous simulation-based separation of factors is commendable, but findings do not translate directly to human diagnostic accuracy or electromagnetic continuum.

comments: DeepHit's near-ideal calibration is superior to RSF and Cox approaches; external validation strengthens findings, though applicability to other regions uncertain.

comments: Framework demonstrates feasibility as explainable triage aid using generation metadata and readability; expert review remains indispensable as model does not assess semantic content.
